_comment: The Ruler Wheel data. Each ruler has regnal years (BCE), a realm, and the dual verdict (biblical vs historical). The wheel auto-spins to the ruler whose reign contains the slider year. 'focus' is an optional bounds box to fly to when selected. Propaganda pairs come from the study library's dual-narrative framing.

rulers.name: Ramesses III
rulers.biblical: One of the unnamed pharaohs behind the exodus traditions.
rulers.historical: Egypt's last great warrior-king — he held off the Sea Peoples and the collapse for one more generation, then the empire in Canaan dissolves.

rulers.name: David
rulers.biblical: The shepherd-king who conquered from Dan to Beersheba, the man after God's own heart.
rulers.historical: A regional warlord who took a small Jebusite town and founded a dynasty — the House of David, confirmed by the Tel Dan Stele within a century of his death.

rulers.name: Solomon
rulers.biblical: The wisest and wealthiest king — 700 wives, fleets of Tarshish, the temple on Mount Moriah.
rulers.historical: A modest king of a small highland town, if he existed as the Bible describes at all; the 'Solomonic' gates are now dated to the 9th century. The temple's structure is real ANE architecture — the grandeur is retrojection.

rulers.name: Jeroboam I
rulers.biblical: 'Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who made Israel to sin' — the golden calves of Dan and Bethel (1 Kgs 12:26-30).
rulers.historical: The founder of the northern kingdom — the 'sin' was setting up legitimate Yahwist shrines outside Jerusalem, which the Judahite scribes condemned to monopolize worship.

rulers.name: Omri
rulers.biblical: 'Omri did what was evil in the sight of the Lord' (1 Kgs 16:25).
rulers.historical: Founder of the dynasty Assyria called the House of Omri for a century. He built Samaria, allied with Phoenicia, and made Israel a regional power.

rulers.name: Ahab
rulers.biblical: 'Ahab did more to provoke the Lord than all the kings of Israel before him' (1 Kgs 16:33) — Jezebel, Baal, and Naboth's vineyard.
rulers.historical: Commander of 2,000 chariots — the largest force in the anti-Assyrian coalition at Qarqar (Kurkh Monolith). A major regional player, not a villain.

rulers.name: Jehu
rulers.biblical: The anointed reformer who wiped out the House of Omri and the Baal cult — rewarded with a dynasty of five (2 Kgs 9-10).
rulers.historical: The coup that ended the Omrides — and submitted Israel to Assyria. The Black Obelisk shows him kneeling before Shalmaneser III.

rulers.name: Jeroboam II
rulers.biblical: 'He did what was evil in the sight of the Lord; he did not depart from all the sins of Jeroboam' (2 Kgs 14:24) — while Amos and Hosea denounce the rich.
rulers.historical: Israel's last golden age: territorial expansion, economic boom, and wealth the prophets could smell. Twenty years after his death, the kingdom is gone.

rulers.name: Tiglath-Pileser III
rulers.biblical: Unnamed directly, but the 'king of Assyria' whose conquests the prophets saw coming (Isa 7-8; 2 Kgs 15:29).
rulers.historical: The empire's reorganizer: provinces, deportations, and the 732 campaign that destroyed Damascus and stripped Israel to a rump.

rulers.name: Sargon II
rulers.biblical: The fall of Samaria and the ten lost tribes happen on his watch (2 Kgs 17).
rulers.historical: He finished what Shalmaneser V started: 'I conquered Samaria and carried away 27,290 people.' His name is the shadow over the north.

rulers.name: Hezekiah
rulers.biblical: The reformer-king: he removes the high places, trusts Yahweh, and the angel saves Jerusalem (2 Kgs 18-19).
rulers.historical: The rebel who paid: Sennacherib's prism records the tribute that stripped the temple of gold. Hezekiah's own Siloam Tunnel survives — water engineering for a siege he barely survived.

rulers.name: Manasseh
rulers.biblical: The worst king of Judah — child sacrifice, idolatry, and the prophets' curse (2 Kgs 21).
rulers.historical: A loyal Assyrian vassal for 55 years — the longest reign in the dynasty, and evidently popular. His success suggests the Yahwist partisans were the minority.

rulers.name: Josiah
rulers.biblical: The reformer who 'found' the Book of the Law, smashed the shrines, and served Yahweh with all his heart (2 Kgs 22-23).
rulers.historical: The reform's engine: a scroll that is almost certainly an early Deuteronomy, centralized worship to Jerusalem, and expanded into the ruins of the north. Then he died at Megiddo in 609.

rulers.name: Nebuchadnezzar II
rulers.biblical: The destroyer of Jerusalem — the rod of the Lord's anger, and the furnace of the exile (Jer 25; Dan 1-4).
rulers.historical: The greatest builder-king of Babylon: Carchemish (605), Jerusalem (597, 586), the hanging gardens' city, and ration tablets that feed Jehoiachin at his table.

rulers.name: Cyrus II
rulers.biblical: Yahweh's 'anointed,' who lets the exiles return and rebuild (Isa 45:1; Ezra 1).
rulers.historical: Founder of the Persian empire: took Media (550) and Babylon (539) without a battle, and issued the return policy recorded on the Cyrus Cylinder.
